title: a flat average lets a wrong answer score well
source: Jarvis itself, 2026-09-03: the first version of scoreRun averaged every dimension evenly, and a run that reproduced the bug, kept its scope tight, opened a tidy pull request and fixed NOTHING scored 0.75. Deleting the failing test scored the same.
objective: score({correct: 0, tidy: 1, scoped: 1, reported: 1, cost: 120000}) returns a high score even though correct is 0, and a run that spent fewer tokens scores higher than one that spent more. A run that did not do the thing must not score well, and cost must not raise the score. Fix score() and add a regression test.
note: Three traps, and a fix that only clears one of them fails the hidden suite. Capping the result when correct is 0 satisfies the complaint as stated and still lets cost dominate. Dropping cost from the average satisfies that and still counts an unmeasured dimension as a zero, so two runs are ranked by whether something happened to be measurable. The bug is that the shape of the calculation is wrong, not that a number is wrong - which is exactly why it took a real iteration to find in the original.
